question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction for platform voice input, and which initial platform flow and security contract should it support?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but implementation requires maintainer intent for native app versus Gateway/media ownership, endpoint/auth handling, private-network policy, fallback behavior, and whether this starts as macOS PTT only or a broader native voice design.

options.title: Design native STT seam first
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native ASR/STT abstraction, start with the smallest approved flow, and reuse tools.media.audio or provider contracts where that is the chosen owner boundary.

options.title: Narrow to macOS PTT slice
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87140 as the first implementation slice while this broader issue remains the design tracker.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native voice input on Apple/Android platform speech until maintainers define the cross-platform privacy, endpoint, and fallback policy.

recommendation.title: Design native STT seam first
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native ASR/STT abstraction, start with the smallest approved flow, and reuse tools.media.audio or provider contracts where that is the chosen owner boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest affected current code path is native macOS voice/PTT, and steipete has the clearest feature-history signal there.
